name: PX4 Autopilot
summary: Dronecode flight stack for multirotors, fixed-wing, VTOL, rovers and boats, built on NuttX with a uORB pub/sub middleware. Its EKF2 estimator fuses IMU, GNSS, baro, magnetometer, optical flow, range finders and external vision.
why_it_matters: The most common permissive-licensed (BSD) autopilot base for defense and commercial UAS; EKF2 external-vision and flow fusion is the standard route to GPS-denied flight.
hackathon_notes: Run `make px4_sitl gz_x500` for SITL with Gazebo in under an hour. Feed VIO/SLAM poses via the ROS 2 uXRCE-DDS bridge or MAVLink ODOMETRY; disable GPS with EKF2_GPS_CTRL to test GPS-denied behaviour.

name: ArduPilot
summary: GPL autopilot covering Copter, Plane (incl. QuadPlane VTOL), Rover, boats and ArduSub, plus AP_Periph CAN peripherals. EKF3 supports switchable source sets, so GNSS, optical flow, beacons, wheel odometry and external vision can be swapped in flight.
why_it_matters: Very broad vehicle coverage and mature non-GPS navigation docs; EKF3 source switching (EK3_SRCn_*) is directly useful for GNSS-loss and spoofing-resilience experiments.
hackathon_notes: `sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter --console --map` gives SITL in minutes. Lua scripting lets you add behaviour on the flight controller without a fork. Use SIM_GPS1_ENABLE=0 / EK3_SRC1_* to simulate GNSS denial.

name: INAV
summary: Navigation-focused fork of the Cleanflight/Betaflight lineage for small multirotors, fixed-wing and rovers, adding GPS position hold, return-to-home and waypoint missions on cheap F4/F7/H7 boards.
why_it_matters: Lowest-cost path to GNSS waypoint navigation on FPV-class airframes; useful to show how small drones behave on GNSS loss and how RTH failsafes work.
hackathon_notes: Configure with INAV Configurator; supports MSP and a MAVLink telemetry subset. SITL exists but is less polished than PX4/ArduPilot. Good for physical demos on cheap hardware.

name: Betaflight
summary: Racing/freestyle-oriented flight controller firmware focused on attitude control and low-latency filtering; GPS rescue mode is its main navigation feature.
why_it_matters: Dominant firmware on FPV drones seen in current conflicts; understanding its limited navigation (GPS Rescue only) matters for C-UAS and EW-impact analysis.
hackathon_notes: Not a navigation platform; use for FPV-class hardware or to study how small drones react to link loss and GNSS jamming.

name: Paparazzi UAV
summary: Long-running academic autopilot (ENAC, TU Delft and others) for fixed-wing, rotorcraft and hybrids, with its own ground segment, flight-plan language and INS modules.
why_it_matters: Strong research heritage in fixed-wing and micro air vehicles, including vision-based and swarm experiments; a non-MAVLink reference architecture.
hackathon_notes: Toolchain and ground station setup takes hours; pick only if you know it already. Flight-plan XML is a nice example of declarative mission logic.

name: LibrePilot
summary: GitHub mirror of LibrePilot, the community continuation of OpenPilot for CC3D/Revolution boards, with the GCS bundled. Main development was on Bitbucket and has been quiet for years.
why_it_matters: Historical reference for the OpenPilot-era INS13 estimator and UAVTalk protocol; not a base for new work.
hackathon_notes: Read-only reference. Hardware is end-of-life.

name: OpenPilot (mirror)
summary: Mirror of the original OpenPilot flight controller project (not comma.ai's openpilot), frozen since 2015.
why_it_matters: Origin of the TauLabs, dRonin and LibrePilot family; historical only.
hackathon_notes: Historical reference only.

name: dRehmFlight VTOL
summary: Single-file Arduino/Teensy flight controller for small VTOL and multirotor craft, written to be read and modified by students.
why_it_matters: Easiest flight-control code to understand end to end; good for teaching attitude estimation (Madgwick) and control loops in a weekend.
hackathon_notes: Flash to a Teensy with an MPU6050/9250 IMU; no navigation or MAVLink, so pair with a companion for anything beyond stabilisation.

name: ESP-Drone
summary: Espressif's mini quadcopter firmware for ESP32/ESP32-S2/S3, derived from Crazyflie code, controlled over Wi-Fi.
why_it_matters: Very cheap, hackable airframe with Wi-Fi control; usable for indoor swarm or RF experiments.
hackathon_notes: Builds with ESP-IDF; supports optical-flow deck style positioning only with extra sensors. Expect tuning effort on DIY frames.

name: Crazyflie firmware
summary: Firmware for the Crazyflie nano quad, Bolt and the Roadrunner positioning tag, with EKF and complementary estimators supporting UWB Loco positioning, Lighthouse, Flow deck and mocap.
why_it_matters: Mature indoor research platform where UWB/Lighthouse localisation and GPS-free estimation are first-class; widely used in swarm papers.
hackathon_notes: If you have Crazyflies, the Python lib gets you scripted flights in an hour. UWB Loco anchors make a good GNSS-denied testbed. Simulation via crazyswarm2 or the official SIL.

name: cflib (Crazyflie Python library)
summary: Python API to connect, log, set parameters and send setpoints/high-level commands to Crazyflies over Crazyradio or USB.
why_it_matters: Fastest way to script autonomy experiments on nano drones.
hackathon_notes: pip install cflib; works without ROS.

name: Crazyswarm2
summary: ROS 2 stack for flying large swarms of Crazyflies, with simulation backends and Python scripting.
why_it_matters: Ready-made multi-agent testbed for coordinated indoor flight and formation experiments.
hackathon_notes: Needs ROS 2 Humble/Jazzy; the sim backend lets you test without hardware.

name: ROSflight firmware
summary: Lean research autopilot (BYU) that keeps only attitude estimation and low-level control on the flight board and pushes everything else to a ROS companion.
why_it_matters: Clean split between embedded and onboard autonomy; good for teams who want full control of the estimator on the companion.
hackathon_notes: Use with rosflight_ros_pkgs; includes a simulator so hardware is optional.

name: ROSflight ROS packages
summary: ROS 2 interface, simulator and utilities for the ROSflight autopilot.
why_it_matters: Companion-side half of ROSflight, where navigation and autonomy live.
hackathon_notes: Start with the sim launch files.

name: PX4 ECL (Estimation & Control Library)
summary: Former standalone home of PX4's EKF2 and related estimation/control code; archived after the code moved into PX4-Autopilot.
why_it_matters: Its history and docs remain a readable reference for the EKF2 derivation (SymPy-generated equations).
hackathon_notes: Read the current EKF2 in PX4-Autopilot src/modules/ekf2 instead; use this for history.

name: PX4 OpticalFlow
summary: Algorithms for computing optical flow from a downward camera to produce velocity inputs for a position estimator.
why_it_matters: Optical flow plus range finder is the cheapest GNSS-free velocity source for low-altitude hover and drift control.
hackathon_notes: Can run on a companion and publish OPTICAL_FLOW_RAD over MAVLink; check activity before depending on it.

name: MAVLink
summary: Message definitions (XML dialects) and the pymavlink-based generator for the MAVLink micro air vehicle protocol, used by PX4, ArduPilot and most GCS tools.
why_it_matters: The lingua franca of open-source UAS; any GCS, companion, Remote ID or C-UAS sensor integration ends up speaking it.
hackathon_notes: Add a custom dialect XML and regenerate bindings to prototype new messages (e.g. a jamming-detection report).

name: MAVLink Developer Guide
summary: Source of the mavlink.io documentation: protocol, microservices (mission, parameters, camera, Open Drone ID) and message reference.
why_it_matters: Canonical reference when wiring new sensors or services over MAVLink.
hackathon_notes: Read the microservice pages before implementing anything stateful.

name: pymavlink
summary: Python MAVLink implementation plus tools for connections, log parsing (DataFlash/tlog) and code generation.
why_it_matters: Quickest path to scripting a vehicle or parsing flight logs to evaluate estimator behaviour under GNSS loss.
hackathon_notes: pip install pymavlink; mavutil.mavlink_connection('udp:...') against SITL works in minutes.

name: MAVSDK
summary: C++ SDK exposing high-level MAVLink plugins (action, mission, offboard, telemetry, camera) with a gRPC server for other languages.
why_it_matters: Clean API for companion-side autonomy against PX4 (and to a degree ArduPilot) without ROS.
hackathon_notes: For hackathon speed use the Python binding: since MAVSDK v4, `pip install mavsdk` installs a native binding built in this repo (sync API in `mavsdk`, asyncio in `mavsdk.asyncio`), with no mavsdk_server process. The older gRPC-based MAVSDK-Python with a bundled mavsdk_server lives on as `mavsdk-grpc`.

name: MAVSDK-Python
summary: Asyncio Python client for MAVSDK that wraps a bundled mavsdk_server.
why_it_matters: Probably the fastest way to script missions or offboard control against PX4 SITL.
hackathon_notes: pip install mavsdk-grpc and import mavsdk_grpc (the PyPI name 'mavsdk' now means the native binding with a different API); examples cover takeoff, missions, offboard velocity.

name: MAVROS
summary: ROS/ROS 2 node bridging MAVLink to ROS topics and services, with GCS proxy; widely used to push vision/SLAM poses into PX4 or ArduPilot.
why_it_matters: Standard glue between ROS-based VIO/SLAM and a flight controller for GPS-denied navigation.
hackathon_notes: Publish to /mavros/vision_pose/pose or odometry topics; mind ENU/NED frame conversions.

name: mavlink-router
summary: Lightweight C++ daemon that routes MAVLink between serial, UDP and TCP endpoints with filtering and logging.
why_it_matters: Typical companion-computer plumbing to share one flight-controller link between GCS, autonomy and loggers.
hackathon_notes: Build with meson; one config file. Run it before attaching multiple clients.

name: mavp2p
summary: Single-binary Go MAVLink router/proxy supporting serial, UDP and TCP with deduplication.
why_it_matters: Zero-dependency alternative to mavlink-router; easy to drop on any companion.
hackathon_notes: Download the release binary and run; no build.

name: gomavlib
summary: Go MAVLink v1/v2 library with dialect generation and multiple transports.
why_it_matters: Good for writing small, robust Go services (telemetry relays, sensor bridges).
hackathon_notes: Go modules; examples for reading/writing messages.

name: rust-mavlink
summary: Rust implementation of MAVLink with generated dialects and serial/UDP/TCP connections.
why_it_matters: Memory-safe option for ground or embedded services.
hackathon_notes: cargo add mavlink.

name: node-mavlink
summary: TypeScript/Node.js MAVLink bindings and tools.
why_it_matters: Handy for web dashboards and Node-based ground tools.
hackathon_notes: npm install; works over serial/UDP/TCP.

name: DroneKit-Python
summary: Older high-level Python API for MAVLink vehicles, built on pymavlink; maintenance has slowed (last push 2024).
why_it_matters: Many tutorials still use it; fine for simple ArduPilot scripts but prefer pymavlink or MAVSDK for new work.
hackathon_notes: Has compatibility issues with recent Python versions; pin Python 3.9/3.10 or avoid.

name: MAVProxy
summary: Command-line, module-based ground station and MAVLink proxy with map, console and many plugins.
why_it_matters: Default SITL console for ArduPilot; scriptable modules make it easy to prototype operator-side tools.
hackathon_notes: Comes with sim_vehicle.py; write a module to add custom displays or alerts (e.g. GNSS anomaly warnings).

name: QGroundControl
summary: Qt/QML cross-platform GCS (desktop, Android, iOS) for PX4 and ArduPilot: setup, mission planning, video and telemetry.
why_it_matters: Most common open GCS; a base for custom operator UIs, including Remote ID display.
hackathon_notes: Use prebuilt binaries for SITL; custom builds take a few hours to set up Qt.

name: Mission Planner
summary: Windows-centric C#/.NET GCS for ArduPilot with deep parameter, log-analysis and mission tooling.
why_it_matters: Feature-richest ArduPilot GCS; the EKF and GPS status views are useful during GNSS-denial tests.
hackathon_notes: Windows best; runs under Mono on Linux/mac with caveats.

name: APM Planner 2
summary: Qt-based cross-platform ArduPilot GCS, now largely in maintenance mode.
why_it_matters: Alternative GCS mainly of historical interest.
hackathon_notes: Prefer QGroundControl or Mission Planner.

name: PX4 Flight Review
summary: Web app for uploading and plotting PX4 ULog flight logs, including estimator innovations and test ratios.
why_it_matters: Fast way to judge whether EKF2 is healthy when fusing a new vision or flow source.
hackathon_notes: Use the hosted instance or run locally with Docker.

name: UAV Log Viewer
summary: Browser-based viewer for ArduPilot DataFlash and MAVLink logs (also reads PX4 ULog), with 3D replay and plotting.
why_it_matters: Quick post-flight review of EKF3 innovations and source switching.
hackathon_notes: Hosted at plot.ardupilot.org; no install.

name: ArduPilot Methodic Configurator
summary: Guided step-by-step parameter configuration tool for ArduPilot vehicles.
why_it_matters: Reduces setup mistakes on new airframes, which matter more than code in short builds.
hackathon_notes: Use when building physical ArduPilot vehicles.

name: px4_msgs
summary: ROS 2 message definitions mirroring PX4 uORB topics, used with the uXRCE-DDS bridge.
why_it_matters: Required to talk to PX4 natively from ROS 2 (e.g. VehicleOdometry for external vision).
hackathon_notes: Match the branch to your PX4 version or messages will mismatch.

name: px4_ros_com
summary: Example ROS 2 nodes and helpers (frame transforms) for interfacing with PX4 over DDS.
why_it_matters: Starting templates for offboard control and sending odometry into PX4.
hackathon_notes: Clone alongside px4_msgs into a colcon workspace.

name: Micro XRCE-DDS Agent
summary: Agent that bridges DDS-XRCE clients on microcontrollers into a full DDS / ROS 2 graph; PX4 and ArduPilot use it for native ROS 2.
why_it_matters: Core link in the PX4 and ArduPilot ROS 2 (DDS) paths.
hackathon_notes: Install via snap or build from source; run MicroXRCEAgent udp4 -p 8888 for SITL.

name: PX4 ROS 2 Interface Library
summary: C++ library for writing PX4 flight modes and navigation-data sources in ROS 2 on a companion computer, registered with PX4 as first-class modes.
why_it_matters: Lets a team ship a custom autonomy mode or inject a local/global position estimate (e.g. a visual geolocalisation fix) cleanly into PX4.
hackathon_notes: Needs recent PX4 (1.15+) and matching px4_msgs; examples include custom modes and external navigation interfaces.

name: ROS2 PX4 Offboard Example
summary: Small example of driving PX4 velocity setpoints from ROS 2 teleop, with SITL launch files.
why_it_matters: Good minimal starter for a ROS 2 offboard demo.
hackathon_notes: Runs against PX4 SITL in about an hour (README pins PX4 release/1.15, ROS 2 Humble, Ubuntu 22.04). The README says the tutorial has moved to ARK-Electronics/ros2_px4_teleop_example (C++, PX4 custom modes); use that for current PX4.

name: ardupilot_ros
summary: ROS 2 integration examples for ArduPilot, including Cartographer-based non-GPS navigation and Nav2 setups.
why_it_matters: Directly targets lidar-SLAM-fed GPS-free flight on ArduPilot.
hackathon_notes: Use with ardupilot_gz for simulation; follow the wiki ROS 2 pages.

name: ardupilot_gz
summary: ROS 2 + Gazebo packages for ArduPilot SITL integration and testing.
why_it_matters: Gives a ready simulated vehicle with lidar/cameras for ROS 2 navigation experiments.
hackathon_notes: Target ROS 2 Humble + Gazebo Harmonic per the README.

name: ardupilot_gazebo
summary: Gazebo Sim plugins and models for ArduPilot SITL vehicles.
why_it_matters: Needed for camera/lidar-equipped simulated vehicles to test vision-based navigation.
hackathon_notes: Build the plugin and set GZ_SIM_SYSTEM_PLUGIN_PATH; then run SITL with -f JSON.

name: PX4 SITL Gazebo Classic
summary: Plugins, models and worlds for PX4 SITL/HITL on Gazebo Classic, including flow, depth and VIO-style sensors.
why_it_matters: Many GPS-denied tutorials still rely on its optical-flow and vision plugins.
hackathon_notes: Gazebo Classic is end-of-life; prefer new Gazebo (PX4-gazebo-models) unless you need a specific plugin.

name: PX4 Avoidance
summary: Archived ROS nodes for local planning, global planning and safe landing using depth sensors with PX4.
why_it_matters: Still a useful reference for obstacle avoidance architectures, but unmaintained.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 only; read for design ideas.

name: Rpanion-server
summary: Web-based companion-computer manager for MAVLink vehicles: telemetry routing, video streaming, logging and network config on Raspberry Pi/Jetson.
why_it_matters: Turnkey companion setup so the team spends time on navigation code rather than plumbing.
hackathon_notes: Flash the prebuilt image to a Pi; manage routing in the browser.

name: BlueOS
summary: Docker-based companion OS from Blue Robotics for ROVs, boats and other vehicles, with extensions, MAVLink routing and web UIs; ArduPilot-centred.
why_it_matters: Strong base for maritime/underwater vehicle builds; extension system makes adding a nav service easy.
hackathon_notes: Flash to a Pi 4; write an extension container for your algorithm.

name: MAVLink Camera Manager
summary: Rust service that exposes cameras as MAVLink camera components and streams video (RTSP/UDP) to GCS.
why_it_matters: Makes onboard cameras discoverable to QGC and BlueOS without custom code.
hackathon_notes: Runs standalone or inside BlueOS.

name: vision_to_mavros
summary: ROS and Python scripts that convert external localisation (fiducials, T265 VIO, SLAM, depth) into MAVROS/MAVLink pose messages, tested on ArduPilot.
why_it_matters: Proven recipe for feeding vision-based localisation into ArduPilot EKF3 for GPS-denied flight; came out of GSoC work.
hackathon_notes: Old (2022) but simple; adapt the non-ROS T265 script to any VIO source.

name: vision_landing
summary: Precision landing using visual fiducial targets, sending LANDING_TARGET messages to ArduPilot.
why_it_matters: Example of vision-based terminal approach for recovery/landing without GNSS accuracy.
hackathon_notes: Needs OpenCV and a camera on the companion; inactive since 2023.

name: OpenHD
summary: Open-source long-range digital HD video and telemetry link over Wi-Fi adapters in monitor mode (wifibroadcast-style), for air and ground units.
why_it_matters: Low-cost resilient video/telemetry downlink for situational awareness; also a reference for link behaviour under interference.
hackathon_notes: Needs supported Wi-Fi cards (RTL8812AU) and SBCs; budget a few hours for imaging.

name: WFB-ng
summary: Long-range packet radio link over raw Wi-Fi injection with FEC, carrying video, MAVLink and IP tunnels.
why_it_matters: Unidirectional broadcast-style link with FEC is more robust to interference than plain Wi-Fi; useful for EW-resilient telemetry experiments.
hackathon_notes: Install on Linux with compatible RTL8812AU/EU cards; key pairs per link.

name: ExpressLRS
summary: Open-source LoRa/FLRC radio control link (2.4 GHz and sub-GHz) with high packet rates, telemetry and MAVLink passthrough modes.
why_it_matters: Dominant open RC link in FPV; its behaviour under jamming and its telemetry options matter for EW-resilience and C-UAS work.
hackathon_notes: Flash with ExpressLRS Configurator; receivers are cheap.

name: mLRS
summary: LoRa-based bidirectional link carrying RC and full MAVLink serial data on 2.4 GHz, 868/915 MHz and 433 MHz.
why_it_matters: Combines control and telemetry over long-range LoRa for ArduPilot/PX4, which is useful where Wi-Fi links fail.
hackathon_notes: Supports several off-the-shelf modules; read the hardware list first.

name: SiK radio firmware
summary: Firmware and tools for Si1000-based telemetry radios (3DR/RFD900 class) carrying MAVLink.
why_it_matters: Classic serial telemetry radio stack; frequency-hopping config is relevant to link robustness.
hackathon_notes: Mostly use stock firmware; configure via AT commands or Mission Planner.

name: ArduRemoteID
summary: ESP32-based Remote ID transmitter firmware implementing ASTM F3411 broadcast (Bluetooth and Wi-Fi) fed from MAVLink or DroneCAN.
why_it_matters: Cheap compliant Remote ID broadcasting, and the transmitter side of any Remote ID-based C-UAS awareness demo.
hackathon_notes: Flash an ESP32-S3/C3 dev board; pair with opendroneid receiver-android to show detection end to end.

name: Open Drone ID Core C
summary: C library to encode and decode Remote ID messages per ASTM F3411 / ASD-STAN EN 4709-002, plus MAVLink wrappers.
why_it_matters: Foundation for building Remote ID transmitters, receivers and sensor integrations.
hackathon_notes: Plain C, easy to embed; includes test vectors.

name: OpenDroneID Android receiver
summary: Example Android app that receives Remote ID over Bluetooth 4/5 and Wi-Fi Beacon/NaN and shows drones on a map.
why_it_matters: Turns a phone into a passive drone detector; quick situational-awareness / C-UAS demo.
hackathon_notes: Install the APK; Wi-Fi NaN support depends on the phone.

name: OpenDroneID Linux transmitter
summary: Example Linux transmitter for Remote ID over Bluetooth and Wi-Fi.
why_it_matters: Lets a companion computer broadcast Remote ID for testing receivers.
hackathon_notes: Inactive since 2023; fine for lab testing.

name: uav_electronic_ids
summary: Arduino classes for several UAV electronic ID formats (ASTM/EU Remote ID, French ID) and UTM interfaces, with ESP32 examples.
why_it_matters: Small, readable alternative Remote ID implementation, including receiver-side sketches.
hackathon_notes: Arduino IDE; inactive since early 2024.

name: DroneCAN libcanard
summary: Minimal C implementation of the DroneCAN protocol used for GNSS, compass, airspeed and other peripherals on CAN.
why_it_matters: Needed to build custom CAN sensors (e.g. an alternative nav sensor) that ArduPilot/PX4 can consume.
hackathon_notes: Use with dronecan/DSDL; mostly for hardware teams.

name: Aerostack2
summary: ROS 2 framework for autonomous single and multi-aerial-robot systems with behaviours, state estimation plugins and platform adapters (PX4, Crazyflie, DJI, Gazebo).
why_it_matters: A complete companion-side autonomy architecture, handy for multi-UAV missions without starting from scratch.
hackathon_notes: Docker images exist; expect a learning curve for its behaviour system.
